triples.subject: Marfa Ignatyevna
triples.quote: Marfa Ignatyevna, the wife of old Grigory, who had been knocked senseless near the fence, was sleeping soundly in her bed and might well have slept till morning

triples.subject: Marfa Ignatyevna
triples.quote: seeing that her master’s window was open and that there was a candle alight in the window, she ran there and began calling Fyodor Pavlovitch.

triples.subject: Olga Mihailovna
triples.quote: so as slyly to startle the eldest granddaughter, Olga Mihailovna, by showing that he knew her secret, that he knew it was her birthday, and that she was trying to conceal it on purpose

triples.subject: Fyodor Pavlovitch Karamazov
triples.quote: Pyotr Ilyitch was met with the astounding news that old Fyodor Pavlovitch really had been murdered that evening in his own house, murdered and robbed.

triples.subject: Mihail Makarovitch Makarov
triples.quote: His widowed daughter lived with him, with her two unmarried daughters, grown-up girls, who had finished their education.

triples.subject: Olga Mihailovna
triples.quote: His widowed daughter lived with him, with her two unmarried daughters, grown-up girls, who had finished their education.

triples.subject: Murder of Fyodor Pavlovitch
triples.quote: Pyotr Ilyitch was met with the astounding news that old Fyodor Pavlovitch really had been murdered that evening in his own house, murdered and robbed.

triples.subject: Mitya
triples.quote: she heard a dreadful scream from their garden, and this was no doubt Grigory’s scream, “Parricide!” uttered when he caught hold of Mitya’s leg.

triples.subject: Marfa Ignatyevna
triples.quote: Terror-stricken, Marfa rushed away from the window, ran out of the garden, drew the bolt of the big gate and ran headlong by the back way to the neighbor, Marya Kondratyevna.

triples.subject: Smerdyakov
triples.quote: The doctor remained at Fyodor Pavlovitch’s to make a post-mortem next day on the body. But he was particularly interested in the condition of the servant, Smerdyakov.

triples.subject: Fyodor Pavlovitch
triples.quote: The deputy police inspector of the town was commissioned to take four witnesses, to enter Fyodor Pavlovitch’s house and there to open an inquiry on the spot

triples.subject: Fyodor Pavlovitch
triples.quote: a big and thick envelope with the inscription: “A present of three thousand roubles for my angel Grushenka, if she is willing to come.”

triples.subject: Dmitri Fyodorovitch
triples.quote: namely, his idea that Dmitri Fyodorovitch would shoot himself before daybreak, that he had resolved to do so, had spoken of it to Ilyitch, had taken the pistols, loaded them before him

triples.subject: Trifon Borissovitch
triples.quote: The box with the pistols had been carried off by Trifon Borissovitch and put in a suitable place.

triples.subject: Dmitri Fyodorovitch
triples.quote: He was instructed to avoid raising the alarm when he reached Mokroe, but to keep constant watch over the “criminal” till the arrival of the proper authorities
